edits.before: Cage online: drop it ON yourself when he engages, behind him when he farms — the geometry does the fighting.
edits.after: His soldiers out-range your Q and zone the wave — cage on yourself when he steps up and concede the poke trade.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Event Horizon (self-cage) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — the shield-dash sits on a 22s cooldown at rank 1 (16s max); the window after he burns it is your commit. - Budget E Event Horizon (20s at rank 1) for emergencies and R for opportunities — never swap them.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: When he walks up to soldier-poke, cage the path back — the edge stun into Dark Matter turns his poke step into a lost trade.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: His Q-W shove out-ranges you; matching it costs the health and mana you owe the curve — thin the wave, stack, don't duel the shove.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Azir wins by kiting with soldiers, eating your burst on Shifting Sands' shield, and walling your retreat with his R.
